transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-03
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Morgan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Anand (Redwood SE), Daniel Park (Lynx Head of Platform), Sara Voss (Lynx Security Lead), Omar Ruiz (Lynx ML Infra)

Auto Summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
- Scoping call to align on POC success criteria, workload sizing for benchmarks, and security/compliance requirements for a 4-week pilot.
- Key security asks: SOC 2 Type II evidence, ISO-27001 summary, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC model, audit logs retention, KMS/HSM integration, VPC connectivity options.
- Benchmarks: target p99 latency < 350ms for 8k token median? (note: sample lengths discussed), throughput target ~80-100 qps burst, consistent 95/99 percentiles.
- Next steps: Redwood to share artifacts; schedule benchmark run; customer to provide sample workload.

Topics identified: success criteria; workload size & seq length; expected traffic patterns; expected SLOs; SOC2/ISO questions; SSO & RBAC; audit/logging retention; encryption/KMS; dedicated vs hosted options; pilot timeline and acceptance criteria.

Transcript:
[00:00] Morgan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. we got about 55 minutes on the calendar, wanted to align on the pilot scope and the security bar, et cetera. Quick intros?
[00:09] Daniel Park: Yep, Dan here, Head of Platform at Lynx, I own infra decisions for model infra, ah, happy to dig in.
[00:13] Sara Voss: Sara — security lead, I'll own compliance questions and ISMS checks.
[00:16] Omar Ruiz: Omar, ML infra, I'll run the benchmarks and work with Priya on scripts.
[00:20] Priya Anand: Hi all, Priya from Redwood, I'm the SE on the engagement — I'll run the benchmark plan and help size the dedicated pools if needed.
[00:27] Morgan Lee: Great. Quick context from Lynx — you mentioned wanting a pilot to validate both performance and security for a customer-facing summarization feature, correct? Maybe you can say a bit about traffic shape.
[00:36] Daniel Park: Yeah, the feature will be used in our analytics UI — roughly 4–5k daily active users, we expect bursty traffic during reports release windows. For the pilot we want to emulate about 10k requests over a week, with spikes up to 80–120 qps for short periods. Typical prompt sizes are median ~450 tokens, heavy tail up to 2k tokens for long docs.
[00:54] Priya Anand: ok that helps. do you have expected SLOs? p95/p99 goals?
[00:58] Daniel Park: We're aiming p95 < 150ms and p99 < 400ms for the generation step; cost is also a concern so we want to compare hosted vs dedicated cost/latency tradeoffs.
[01:07] Morgan Lee: understood. quick flag — p95 150ms on heavier sequences may be ambitious on some open models, we'll document tradeoffs. For pilot, would acceptance be a comparison across 2 model configs and a clear cost per 1k tokens number?
[01:18] Daniel Park: Exactly — success criteria: 1) meets latency targets for the 80% median workload, 2) throughput at expected burst levels for 10-minute windows, 3) no security blockers — SOC2 evidence + SSO integration proof-of-concept.
[01:30] Sara Voss: on security, our checklist: SOC 2 Type II report, ISO 27001 posture statement, SAML SSO with our IdP (Okta), fine-grained RBAC, audit logs with immutable retention for 1 year, KMS/HSM for key management, encryption at rest and in transit, plus data residency notes.
[01:48] Morgan Lee: That's a solid list. We can share SOC2 Type II artifact and ISO summary. For SAML, Redwood supports SAML 2.0 IdP flows; we typically do a test integration in the pilot. For RBAC we provide role templates and token-scoped permissions, and audit logs are available via the Console or delivered to your SIEM via syslog/S3 (we'll confirm retention options).
[02:08] Priya Anand: For encryption and KMS, we support customer-managed keys through AWS KMS and HSM integrations on private deployments. In hosted we offer envelope encryption with BYOK options. But full HSM-backed keys on-prem or dedicated private is also possible.
[02:23] Omar Ruiz: small question — can we get raw request/response logs for debugging? For privacy we want redaction options.
[02:28] Priya Anand: Yes, we can provide request/response logs for the pilot in a secure S3 with redaction rules; default retention is 30 days in hosted but can be extended for the pilot, and we can provide PII redaction patterns as config.
[02:40] Daniel Park: ok sounds good. On network connectivity — we need a VPC peering or PrivateLink option for pilot traffic. Is that available?
[02:46] Morgan Lee: Yes, VPC peering and PrivateLink are supported for Dedicated and Private deployments. Hosted can use TLS-only public endpoints but we can put a VPC egress path if needed — we will outline best fit.
[02:56] Sara Voss: Another ask: audit trails should include token-level cost breakdowns for chargeback. Can you show an example?
[03:02] Priya Anand: We'll include screenshots of the Console billing by token and exports. For the pilot we can also provide daily CSV exports of token usage by project/route.
[03:10] Daniel Park: For benchmarks — what tooling do you prefer? we typically use k6 for load, but if you have a script that's more representative that'll help.
[03:16] Priya Anand: We use a k6 + python wrapper internally for controlled sequence lengths and KV cache warmup. We'll share the runbook; typical steps: 1) warm KV cache with prefix traffic, 2) run steady-state at target qps for 10–15 minutes, 3) run burst test for 10-minute spikes, 4) collect p50/p95/p99 and throughput.
[03:33] Omar Ruiz: cool. For samples we'll include worst-case long docs and median 450 token prompts. Also want to test prefix caching savings for repeated user conversations.
[03:42] Priya Anand: Great. How many concurrent conversations per user do you expect?
[03:46] Daniel Park: Typically 1–2 active per user, but concurrency across users during peak may hit 120 qps.
[03:52] Morgan Lee: noted. For sizing, rough starting point: if median 450 tokens and ~40 tokens/sec effective, that implies CPU/GPU token throughput numbers — but we'll size based on model choices. Are you open to testing an Llama-2 70B quantized variant and a smaller 13B to compare cost/latency?
[04:09] Daniel Park: yes we want a comparison. Also whether Redwood's Dedicated offers reserved GPU pools that can hit the p99 targets?
[04:15] Priya Anand: Dedicated pools with A10x/80s style cards can consistently support lower latency and more predictable p99s. We'll propose two configs in the runbook: hosted (multi-tenant) with autoscale and a dedicated 4-GPU pool for the pilot.
[04:27] Sara Voss: On compliance — how do you handle data deletion for pilot data post-eval? We need proof we can purge logs and backups within X days.
[04:33] Morgan Lee: We support documented data deletion procedures; for hosted we can trigger deletions and provide audit of deletion events. For Private/on-prem we of course control retention. We'll include deletion SLA options in the doc.
[04:43] Daniel Park: For the pilot, can we run a scoped breach and incident response tabletop? Sara wants to know RTO for alerts.
[04:48] Sara Voss: yeah tabletop would be helpful.
[04:50] Priya Anand: We can do a short 30-min security walkthrough or tabletop with your team during the pilot window.
[04:55] Omar Ruiz: Benchmarks — are there any sample numbers you can share from a similar customer? even ballpark p99 numbers for 512 tokens?
[05:01] Priya Anand: Ballpark, for a quantized Llama-2 70B on Dedicated we've seen p95 ~80–150ms and p99 ~200–500ms for shorter sequences (<=512) depending on batching. For hosted multi-tenant numbers are higher and vary. We'll attach anonymized benchmark snippets.
[05:17] Daniel Park: Ok that frames it. I'd like explicit cost per 1k tokens for each config so we can run ROI.
[05:22] Morgan Lee: We'll produce cost estimates in the commercial appendix of the pilot proposal — both per-token and flat reserved pricing.
[05:28] Sara Voss: On SSO — we use Okta. We expect SAML 2.0, SCIM for provisioning would be nice. Also require SSO login to the Console to map to RBAC roles.
[05:38] Priya Anand: We support SAML 2.0 and SCIM provisioning; RBAC ties into SSO identity. We'll provide a mapping template so you can define groups and minimal roles for the pilot.
[05:48] Daniel Park: Any pen test or third-party attestation details we should be aware of?
[05:52] Morgan Lee: We have third-party pentest summaries and SOC2 Type II; we'll include high-level findings. For detailed pentest results we can provide a scope summary under NDA.
[06:02] Sara Voss: Good. Regarding logs shipped to our SIEM — can you confirm formats (jsonl/syslog) and maximum throughput?
[06:09] Priya Anand: We support JSONL to S3 and syslog streaming to your SIEM. Throughput depends on retention granularity but the pilot shouldn't hit limits; we'll include recommended batching and compression.
[06:19] Omar Ruiz: timeline check — we'd like to run pilot across 4 weeks and decide on dedicated after week 3 based on metrics. Is that workable?
[06:26] Morgan Lee: Yes, typical pilot cadence is 3–6 weeks. For acceptance we'll lay out weekly checkpoints and one final acceptance review.
[06:33] Daniel Park: ok good. Can we walk through a proposed acceptance criteria doc now?
[06:36] Morgan Lee: Sure — propose acceptance criteria: 1) Functional parity for target feature; 2) Performance — p95/p99 thresholds for median workload met in at least 3 of 4 weekly runs; 3) Security — SOC2 artifacts reviewed, SSO test passes, audit logs demonstrate retention and access; 4) Cost — total cost per 1k tokens within the agreed budget delta vs baseline.
[06:58] Sara Voss: Curious about RBAC granularity — can we restrict token issuance and route-level permissions? We need admin, ops, auditor roles, and an automation service account.
[07:06] Priya Anand: Yes, route-level permissions and service accounts are supported. We'll share the RBAC model: admin (full), engineer (deploy/monitor), auditor (read-only logs & billing), service (token limited to certain routes).
[07:16] Morgan Lee: Do you require offline key escrow or HSM auditing?
[07:19] Sara Voss: We prefer HSM-backed key storage for production; for pilot KMS BYOK is sufficient but note our preference.
[07:25] Priya Anand: Understood. We'll document BYOK and HSM options and the steps to upgrade.
[07:29] Daniel Park: Any data residency constraints? Our customers are EU-heavy; we'd prefer EU region for inference.
[07:35] Morgan Lee: We have EU regions available for both Hosted and Dedicated; for Private we can deploy inside customer VPC/region. We'll call out region options in the pilot plan.
[07:44] Omar Ruiz: For the benchmark scripts, can the runbook include KV cache warmup recipe? That's important for repeated conversation flows.
[07:51] Priya Anand: Absolutely — we'll include precise commands: prefill keys for N users, run warmup at 20 qps for 30 minutes, then start the steady-state.
[07:58] Daniel Park: Anything special for rate-limiting behaviors? We need 429 handling and graceful degradation.
[08:03] Priya Anand: We'll show fallback policies, retry guidance, and circuit-breaker recommendations. Redwood supports automatic fallback to cheaper model variants if high latency detected.
[08:13] Sara Voss: Can you provide an audit trail of who initiated rollbacks in the console? We need tamper-evidence.
[08:18] Morgan Lee: Yes, rollouts and config changes are tracked with user and timestamp, and we can provide immutable logs for audit.
[08:25] Daniel Park: ok great. A quick note on acceptance: We want the pilot to include a short business-level report after week 2 and week 4 with metrics and recommendations.
[08:33] Morgan Lee: We'll deliver those check-ins.
[08:36] Omar Ruiz: On benchmarks — we also want to test cold-start latencies for new shards. Include a cold-start test?
[08:41] Priya Anand: Yes, we'll include a cold-start test and warm vs cold comparisons.
[08:45] Daniel Park: Good. Anything else from Redwood on security artifacts?
[08:49] Priya Anand: We'll attach an NDA-bound pentest summary if needed, SOC2 Type II, ISO statement, the SAML/SCIM integration guide, and the RBAC template.
[08:58] Sara Voss: ok please send those links. Also please include a data flow diagram that shows where PII is stored and who has access.
[09:05] Morgan Lee: We'll include a redacted DFD for the pilot.
[09:08] Daniel Park: Let's recap next steps — I'll list what we need from you: runbook, SOC2, sample payloads, SSO config details. We also want a kickoff benchmark slot.
[09:18] Morgan Lee: Confirmed. We'll share SOC2 and ISO artifacts by Monday (Oct 6), Priya will send runbook by Oct 7, and we'll propose benchmark times for week of Oct 13.
[09:27] Sara Voss: We'll aim to provide sample payloads and Okta SAML metadata by Oct 10.
[09:32] Omar Ruiz: I'll be on the benchmark run and will share the load test environment access.
[09:36] Priya Anand: Sounds good. I'll draft the benchmark test plan right after this call and include commands and expected outputs so you can validate.
[09:44] Morgan Lee: Any blockers?
[09:45] Daniel Park: none immediate. Sara wants to review SOC2 but that's standard.
[09:49] Sara Voss: I'll review docs but may have follow-ups about log retention.
[09:53] Morgan Lee: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with artifacts and a proposed schedule.
[09:59] End of recording.
